extracted.intended_audience: journalists and public relations practitioners; press-release writers
extracted.subtask_description: A shared rubric for assessing the news quality of press releases based on eight dimensions journalists and PR practitioners agree on (accuracy, interest, usefulness, completeness, timeliness, subject depiction, mechanics, and news style). Intended to guide writing and selection of releases likely to be picked up by media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifiable facts; correct names, titles, numbers; no errors of fact; no misleading framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that all factual assertions can be verified and that names/titles/numbers are correct. Penalize any factual errors or misleading framing. Scoring (implicit): 5 = all facts verifiable; 1 = errors found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest to Reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Captures attention; has a story angle that engages; goes beyond a mere announcement; has emotional or practical relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the lead/angle grabs attention and offers an engaging news hook rather than a bland announcement. Consider emotional and practical relevance to intended readers. Scoring: 5 = grabbing/compelling; 1 = boring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness to Reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides actionable information; answers reader questions; affects reader's life; has practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the release conveys clear, actionable information or answers likely reader questions (who, what, when, where, why, how) and demonstrates practical relevance. Scoring: 5 = clear value/usefulness; 1 = none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: All necessary information present; 5Ws + H answered; context provided; background available; sources identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify presence of the essential facts (who/what/when/where/why/how), adequate context and background, and identification of sources. Missing core information lowers the score. Scoring: 5 = complete; 1 = gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness of release; aligned with the news cycle; distributed in time for journalists' deadlines; embargo timed appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the timing fits the news cycle and journalists' deadlines, and whether any embargo is set and timed appropriately. Late or premature releases score poorly. Scoring: 5 = perfect timing; 1 = stale or premature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favorable Depiction of Subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject portrayed in the best legitimate light; spokespersons quoted appropriately; context that supports subject. (Primarily a PR concern.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the release presents the subject positively but legitimately — appropriate quotes, supportive context, and avoidance of overt puffery. Balance is important. Scoring: 5 = balanced and appropriate; 1 = puffery or inappropriate depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical / Grammatical Correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper grammar; AP style adherence; correct punctuation; spelling; format conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for grammar, spelling, punctuation, and adherence to style conventions (e.g., AP). Mechanical errors reduce usability and credibility. Scoring: 5 = error-free; 1 = multiple/serious errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Story Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of standard news structure: inverted pyramid, lead with news, supporting paragraphs, quotes, and standard news-article structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the release follows a newswriting structure that makes it easy for journalists to use — strong lead, logical supporting paragraphs, pertinent quotes, and clear structure. Scoring: 5 = textbook/newsworthy structure; 1 = improper or non-news structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit scoring rubric / Total score interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Score each of the eight dimensions 1–5 and sum to a total out of 40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-dimension guidance: Accuracy (5 = all facts verifiable; 1 = errors found), Interest (5 = grabbing; 1 = boring), Usefulness (5 = clear value; 1 = none), Completeness (5 = complete; 1 = gaps), Timeliness (5 = perfect; 1 = stale/premature), Subject depiction (5 = balanced; 1 = puffery), Mechanical (5 = perfect; 1 = errors), News style (5 = textbook; 1 = improper). Total interpretation: 40 = exemplary; 30+ = good; 20–29 = needs work; <20 = poor.
